text:
maria: Quick question — we need to finalize who owns warmup/prewarm credits and the admission policy when a tenant can use both shared and dedicated pools. TL;DR: who mints/consumes tokens and what does the operator vs control-plane contract look like?

ben: Short answer: operator enforces physical allocation (GPUs/slots) and control-plane issues budget/credits. But edgecases: prewarm failures, cross-pool spillovers, and credit reconciliation.

rafael: Agree. We also need a deterministic fallback path when the operator can't honor a prewarm (node boot slow, quota exceeded). Apps need clear SLOs: either immediate degraded-mode admission (higher latency) or queued admission with a timeout.

song: One idea: split responsibilities — control-plane keeps a ledger of warmup credits per tenant and a desired prewarm intent. Operator exposes a very small admission surface: AcceptIntent(intent_id, min_slots, max_slots, ttl) and ReportAllocation(intent_id, allocated_slots). That keeps operator simple.

liu: That sounds clean. Can we sketch the minimal protocol so we all mean the same thing? I wrote a tiny pseudo-API: 
```
// control-plane -> operator
POST /intents 
body: {"intent_id":"i-123","tenant":"acme","min_slots":2,"max_slots":8,"ttl_s":120,"priority":"standard"}

// operator -> control-plane
POST /allocations 
body: {"intent_id":"i-123","allocated":3,"nodes":["gpu-23","gpu-24"]}

// operator will also emit events: allocation_failed, allocation_partial, allocation_ready
```

maria: Nice. A few clarifications: 1) who decrements the tenant's warmup credit balance? 2) what semantics does allocated==0 mean? 3) how do we handle shared headroom so credits can be borrowed between tenants?

ben: Proposal: control-plane mints and decrements credits when it sends the intent (optimistic debit). Operator only checks hard constraints (node feasibility, cluster headroom) and then reports allocation. If operator fails, control-plane refunds the optimistic debit. allocated==0 -> treat as failure event, fall back to degraded route.

rafael: Optimistic debit is fine but it couples the control-plane budget with operator availability. To avoid double-spend, operator should have a short-lived reservation token returned on accept that the control-plane uses to finalize the debit. Flow: 
1) control-plane POST /intents -> operator returns reservation_token if node feasible 
2) control-plane finalize debit -> commit(token) 
3) operator allocates and emits allocation_ready.

song: That adds another round trip but gives strong correctness. We should keep the token TTL small (e.g., 30s) and allow control-plane to retry. Also: for shared pools we may want a "soft borrow" path: control-plane can request borrowable credits from a shared pool; operator enforces per-tenant throttles.

liu: For audit and billing simplicity, I prefer control-plane-centric billing (control-plane records usage events once allocation_ready arrives). That way refunds are simple when allocation_failed is emitted.

maria: We still need to decide admission policy when a tenant has both shared and dedicated pools: prefer dedicated first (predictable), then spill to shared if allowed by tenant policy. Also tenant config should include "spill_allowed":true/false and "max_shared_fraction":0.25.

ben: Implementation detail: control-plane should attach a preference in the intent, e.g., {"preferred_pool":"dedicated","fallback_pool":"shared"}. Operator can honor preference if resources exist. If not, operator returns allocation_partial or allocation_failed.

rafael: Edgecase: Tenant has reserved dedicated capacity but uses up warmup credits quickly — we need a backpressure mechanism to prevent noisy tenants from consuming their dedicated pool's burst credits and starving others. Options: token rate-limiter in control-plane per-tenant + operator-enforced per-pool fairness.

song: Yes. Two-layer approach: control-plane enforces global budgeting and rates; operator enforces physical fairness (max per-tenant slots on a node, preemption windows). That lets operator remain stateless-ish w.r.t long-lived budgets.

liu: Thoughts on metrics/events we need to observe for rollouts: intent_accepted, reservation_issued, allocation_ready, allocation_partial, allocation_failed, allocation_released, refund_issued. Also expose reasons: "node-start-delay", "quota-exceeded", "preempted".

maria: Good list. For the rollout plan: start with optimistic-debit + operator acceptance (no reservation token) in canary; if we see frequent refunds, flip to reservation-token flow. Keep logs verbose for 2 weeks to tune TTLs.

ben: One more: prewarm credit accounting when a tenant owns a dedicated pool but wants to burst into shared — who gets billed? I think control-plane bills the tenant for the burst, but operator tags allocation events with pool_type so downstream billing charges correctly.

rafael: Also include a safety net: operator can trigger a circuit-breaker if more than X allocation_failures per minute to avoid thundering restarts. Send alerts to #eng-runtime with attach: intent_id + failure_reason. deploy-bot should handle that.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] alert hook sketch: 
- on allocation_failed emit to #eng-runtime: "prewarm failed" with intent_id + reason + tenant.
- scheduled task to surface top 10 failing tenants/hour.

maria: OK next steps (action items):
- ben to draft a one-pager with the reservation-token vs optimistic-debit tradeoffs and recommended defaults (token_ttl=30s, intent_ttl=120s) — due EOD friday.
- rafael to prototype small local operator shim that accepts intents and returns reservation_token + simulated allocation events.
- song + liu to draft monitoring and billing event schemas (use the metric list above).

song: I'll start the monitoring schema PR and include fields: event, intent_id, tenant, allocated, pool_type, reason, latency_ms.

liu: Will sketch billing attachment: allocation_ready -> invoiceable_event with pool_type and node_hours approximation.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees an obvious gap call it out here. Otherwise we'll capture this in the follow-up RFC notes and the action items. :thumbsup:

ben: No gaps from me — one nit: add a field in intent for "acceptable_latency_ms" so operator can prefer warm nodes.

maria: Good call, adding that to the one-pager. 

rafael: I'll wire up a tiny simulator for the reservation-token flow and post logs tomorrow.

song: Posting a quick mockup of the intent schema in the PR in a bit.

maria: Great. Closing loop here — we'll reconvene after the canary starts.
